You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

with sync_playwright() as p:

    page = browser.new_page()
    
    page.goto('https://openreview.net/search?content=forum&query=ICLR+2025&term=ICLR.cc/2025/Conference&depth=20&sort=number:asc', wait_until='networkidle')
    page.wait_for_timeout(5000)

        text = link.text_content().strip()[:100]

import json, re

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    context = browser.new_context(user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36')
    page = context.new_page()
    
    # Go to a specific paper page to see if we can get data
    # ICLR accepted papers should be at /forum/{id}
    # Let's try to find a known ICLR 2025 paper ID
    
    # First try the search page - it should render content
    page.goto('https://openreview.net/search?content=forum&query=ICLR+2025&term=ICLR.cc/2025/Conference&depth=20&sort=number%3Aasc', wait_until='networkidle')
    page.wait_for_timeout(5000)
    
    # Get the full HTML and look for data
    html = page.content()
    
    # Look for inline data in script tags
    # Check for __NEXT_DATA__ or window.__data__
    next_data = re.findall(r'window\.__NEXT_DATA__\s*=\s*(?:JSON\.parse\s*\(\s*)?({.*?})\s*(?:\)|;)', html, re.DOTALL)
    if next_data:
        print(f'Found __NEXT_DATA__ ({len(next_data[0])} chars)')
        try:
            data = json.loads(next_data[0])
            print(f'Top keys: {list(data.keys())}')
        except:
            print('Could not parse __NEXT_DATA__')
    
    # Also check for data in __next_f arrays
    next_f = re.findall(r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[0\]\)\s*(.*?)', html, re.DOTALL)
    if next_f:
        print(f'Found __next_f with {len(next_f)} entries')
        # Check last entry for data
        last = next_f[-1] if next_f else ''
        print(f'Last __next_f snippet: {last[:500]}')
    
    # Get all text content
    body_text = page.text_content('body')
    print(f'\nBody text length: {len(body_text)}')

        if keyword in body_text:
            idx = body_text.index(keyword)
            context = body_text[max(0, idx-100):idx+200]
            print(f'\nContext for "{keyword}": {context}')
    
    browser.close()

from curl_cffi import requests as curl_req
import json

# Get the search page HTML to see what API calls it uses
html = curl_req.get(
    'https://openreview.net/search?content=forum&query=&depth=0&limit=5&sort=number%3Aasc',
    impersonate='chrome124'
).text

# Look for API calls or data in the page
import re

# Look for __NEXT_DATA__
matches = re.findall(r'<script[^>]*id="__NEXT_DATA__"[^>]*>(.*?)</script>', html, re.DOTALL)
if matches:
    data = json.loads(matches[0])
    print('Found __NEXT_DATA__')
    # Look for initial state
    props = data.get('props', {}).get('pageProps', {})
    print(f'Props keys: {list(props.keys())}')
    if props.get('initialState'):
        print(f'Initial state keys: {list(props["initialState"].keys())}')
        search_state = props['initialState'].get('search', {})
        print(f'Search state: {json.dumps(search_state, indent=2)[:3000]}')
else:
    print('No __NEXT_DATA__ found')
    # Look for script tags with data
    scripts = re.findall(r'<script[^>]*>(.*?)</script>', html, re.DOTALL)
    for s in scripts[:5]:
        if 'fetch' in s or 'api' in s or 'notes' in s:
            print(f'\nScript with fetch/api: {s[:500]}')
            break

        impersonate='chrome124'
    )

from curl_cffi import requests as curl_req
import json, time

session = curl_req.Session()

# Get session cookies from web page
session.get('https://openreview.net', impersonate='chrome124')

def search_papers(query, target_invitations, limit=100, max_offset=10000):
    results = []
    for offset in range(0, max_offset, limit):
        r = session.get(
            'https://api.openreview.net/notes/search',
            params={'query': query, 'type': 'query', 'limit': limit, 'offset': offset, 'source': 'all'},
            impersonate='chrome124'
        )
        data = r.json()
        notes = data.get('notes', [])
        if not notes:
            print(f'  Empty at offset {offset}')
            break
        
        for n in notes:
            inv = n.get('invitation', '')
            for target in target_invitations:
                if target in inv:
                    results.append(n)
                    break
        
        if len(notes) < limit:
            print(f'  Last batch at {offset} ({len(notes)} notes)')
            break
    
    return results

# Target conference invitations

def make_api_call(page, url):
    return page.evaluate(f'''\nasync () => {{\n    try {{\n        const r = await fetch('{url}', {{credentials: 'same-origin'}});\n        return JSON.parse(await r.text());\n    }} catch(e) {{ return {{error: e.message}}; }}\n}}\n''')

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    context = browser.new_context(user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/125.0.0.0 Safari/537.36')
    page = context.new_page()
    
    # Navigate to homepage
    page.goto('https://openreview.net', wait_until='networkidle')
    page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
    
    # Paginate through all results
    conferences = {
        'ICLR 2025': 'ICLR.cc/2025/Conference',
        'ICML 2024': 'ICML.cc/2024/Conference', 
        'NeurIPS 2024': 'NeurIPS.cc/2024/Conference'
    }
    
    target_invitations = {
        'ICLR 2025': 'ICLR.cc/2025/Conference/-/Blind_Submission',
        'ICML 2024': 'ICML.cc/2024/Conference/-/Blind_Submission',
        'NeurIPS 2024': 'NeurIPS.cc/2024/Conference/-/Blind_Submission'
    }
    
    papers_by_conf = {k: [] for k in conferences}
    
    for offset in range(0, 10000, 100):
        url = f'https://api.openreview.net/notes/search?query=ICLR&limit=100&offset={offset}&source=all'
        result = make_api_call(page, url)
        
        notes = result.get('notes', [])
        if not notes:
            print(f'Empty at offset {offset}')
            break
        
        for n in notes:
            inv = n.get('invitation', '')
            for conf_name, conf_inv in target_invitations.items():
                if conf_inv in inv:
                    papers_by_conf[conf_name].append(n)
        
        if offset % 1000 == 0:
            total = sum(len(v) for v in papers_by_conf.values())
            print(f'Offset {offset}: {len(notes)} notes, {total} papers found')
        
        if len(notes) < 100:
            print(f'Last batch at offset {offset}')
            break
    
    # Print counts
    print('\nPaper counts by conference:')
    for conf, papers in papers_by_conf.items():
        print(f'  {conf}: {len(papers)}')
        
        # Show first paper details
        if papers:
            p = papers[0]
            print(f'    First: {p.get("content", {}).get("title", "?")[:60]}')
            print(f'    Authors: {p.get("authors", [])[:3]}')
            print(f'    Venue: {p.get("content", {}).get("venue", "?")}')
    
    browser.close()
